title: Russell Crowe's A Beautiful Mind Request Added $1 Million to Production
excerpt:
Ron Howard says filming in story order cost the studio an additional million dollars.
He still believes the approach helped Crowe deliver the film's demanding central performance.
body_md:
Ron Howard has revisited Russell Crowe's request to shoot A Beautiful Mind in chronological story order, a departure from the usual practice of organizing scenes around locations, cast availability and production costs. Crowe believed the film's depiction of mathematician John Nash would benefit from a continuous emotional and psychological progression.

The actor was concerned that filming the third act before the opening scenes could make it harder to calibrate how Nash's experience and the audience's understanding of his condition evolved. Howard came to agree with that assessment, even though the approach required him to persuade the studio to accept a more expensive schedule.

Shooting in sequence required two separate trips to Princeton, New Jersey, adding approximately $1 million to the budget. Howard maintains that the extra expense was worthwhile and credits Crowe with delivering the detailed performance the unusual production plan was intended to support.

Released in 2001, A Beautiful Mind went on to win four Academy Awards, including Best Picture, Best Director for Howard, Best Adapted Screenplay and Best Supporting Actress for Jennifer Connelly. A new 4K restoration has also been scheduled for a theatrical anniversary engagement marking twenty-five years since the original release.
